column3: “Of Egypt” is rendered “To Egypt”; “struck down” becomes “defeated.”
NASB uses past and present tenses; “crushed” is rendered “defeated.”
“The River” is rendered “the Nile,” and “earth” as “that land.”
“Virgin of the daughter” is rendered “virgin daughter.”
“They will hear” is rendered as past, “have heard.”
NASB follows the Hebrew; the LXX reads “Why has Apis fled?”
“He will multiply one who stumbles” is rendered “They have repeatedly stumbled.”
“Noise” is rendered “a big noise”; the meaning of the name-wordplay is uncertain.
“Calves of the stall” is rendered “fattened calves.”
“Like the snake which goes” is rendered “moves along like a serpent.”
“Amon from Thebes” is rendered “Amon of Thebes.”
“Make complete destruction” is rendered “make a full end.”
